condition: small clear fluid friction blister on posterior heel from stiff walking shoes
level_rationale: A small 1 cm friction blister on the back of the right heel filled with clear fluid the day after walking 5 miles in stiff new walking shoes is an uncomplicated minor skin blister appropriate for over-the-counter protective ointment self-care, whereas cloudy yellow pus draining from the same heel blister indicates localized secondary bacterial wound infection requiring an outpatient doctor visit.

reference_facts.text: Walked 5 miles in stiff new walking shoes yesterday
Developed a 1 cm friction blister on the back of the right heel
The blister contains clear fluid today

swap_note: Single continuous 15-word vs 17-word span swap after 'I walked 5 miles in stiff new walking shoes yesterday and ' and before ' today so I just need some'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care dermatologic register swap ('friction bulla on my posterior right heel containing clear serous fluid' vs 'friction blister on the back of my right heel filled with clear fluid') + single-fact blister-exudate escalation control (-cf, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses three atomic facts (5-mile walk in stiff new walking shoes yesterday, 1 cm right posterior heel blister, and clear blister fluid today) with a 15-word vs 17-word continuous span swap and 6 identical trailing tokens. Swapping only atomic fact f3 from 'filled with clear fluid' to 'draining cloudy yellow pus' keeps every surrounding fact coherent while shifting care one step from over-the-counter protective ointment self-care (level 1) to outpatient physician wound care (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5 and reviewer_notes.md Rule A) with zero stated negatives.
